title: The $\pi$-property of a Banach space along a filter: reduction to an analytic filter (Theorem B)
author: Tomasz Kania and Jaros{\l}aw Swaczyna
work: The $\pi$-property of a Banach space along a filter
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is one of the three main theorems that the note advertises in its Introduction, and its proof is a complete descriptive set-theoretic argument rather than a citation. Supplying the note's own definition of the F-pi-property and of an F-pi-basis, its definition of convergence along a filter and its discussion of analytic filters as context, the proof still has to encode the witnessing sequence (P_n) as a family of sets: it defines the family A of all supersets of the sublevel sets of the maps x -> ||P_n x - x||, checks A is contained in the given filter F, shows A generates a filter F', proves that A is analytic by writing it as the projection onto the Cantor set coordinate of an intersection of the sets B_n, which are open precisely because each P_n is continuous, then writes the generated filter F' itself as a countable union of projections of closed conditions on tuples (A, A_1, ..., A_n), so that F' is analytic, and finally observes that A is contained in F' and F' is contained in F, which makes (P_n) witness the F'-pi-property. The two analyticity computations - the projection of the intersection of the open sets B_n, and the projection formula for the filter generated by A - are the substance of the theorem and are not asked for in qualifying examinations; the argument is nevertheless short and uses no external theory beyond the definition of an analytic set, which places it in the upper qualifying-to-research range: H2.
